newsitem.title: USA: American Express sells charge receivables.
newsitem.headline: American Express sells charge receivables.

text.p: American Express Co said its American Express Travel Related Services Co is selling $950 million of one series of accounts receivables and $300 million of another.

The $950 million of series 1996-1 class A floating rate accounts receivable certificates have a seven year maturity and are being sold at par to yield one month LIBOR plus 15 basis points to investors, American Express said.

The series 1996-2 class A floating rate accounts receivable trust certificates have a five-year maturity and are being sold at par to yield one month LIBOR plus 12 basis points to investors, American Express said.

The securitization includes receivables generated from a portfolio of American Express cards, but does not include receivables from the its corporate cards or its Optima accounts, American Express said.
Lehman Brothers is leading the group of underwriters of the offering, American Express said.
